summary: Well-executed, fully preregistered autonomous paired trial of a Generate→Verify→Repair (GVR) pipeline for intent-to-configuration safety using gpt-5-mini. The experiment, artifacts, preregistration, and disclosure are complete and reproducible; statistical analysis is appropriate and honestly reports a near-null result (paired increase = 0.0202; exact McNemar p=0.5; 95% bootstrap CI [0.000,0.0505]). The manuscript frames limitations and release of artifacts clearly. Several clarifications and minor but substantive reporting additions are required before finalisation.
required_revisions: Report the exact number of intents flagged as contaminated and excluded from the preregistered primary analysis (and show the paired contingency table including/excluding those items). Include the preregistered sensitivity analysis results (complete-case and contamination-included worst-case imputations) in the manuscript or clearly point to file paths + hashes and summarise numeric outcomes in the Results section.

Provide an explicit, concise operational definition of “emulator-confirmed safety violation” in Methods (what emulator checks were run end-to-end; what constitutes confirmation vs. a verifier false positive), and state how verifier flags were mapped to emulator tests and scoring rules.

Summarise the verifier rule-set coverage (concrete predicates implemented) and give one short representative example of a verifier flag plus the repair prompt injected to the LLM (the full artifacts may remain archived, but the manuscript must include at least one concrete example).

State the exact count of repair attempts and their outcomes in the Results (how many guarded episodes invoked the repair call; distribution and reconciliation with the repair-iteration figure), and report the paired latency/throughput secondary results numerically or reference precise artifact paths and give a short numeric summary in-text.
optional_revisions: Add a short recalculated post-hoc power discussion given the observed baseline success rate and illustrate required N for detecting smaller absolute changes (e.g., 5–10 percentage points).
Report alternative exact-test variants (mid-p or continuity-corrected) as exploratory reanalyses and reference the archived analysis container reproducing them.
Condense Related Work slightly and move one concrete verification implementation detail into a small table to free space while keeping the five-page limit.
